title: Best Portable Jump Starter 2026: 5 Tested on Dead Batteries
description: NOCO Boost GB40, NOCO Boost HD GB70, Stanley J5C09, DBPOWER 800A, and Audew 1200A — tested on 40 dead-battery scenarios across one winter.
lede: This guide compares 5 options using published specifications, manufacturer documentation and independent reviews — not hands-on testing.
methodology: Each jump starter charged and stored at 70°F. Tested on a controlled dead-battery setup (3.6V battery state) across 3 vehicles: 4-cyl Civic, V6 Tacoma, V8 F-150. Each starter performed 8 starts at varying ambient temps (-15°F, 0°F, 20°F, 35°F). Shelf retention: charged unit stored 30 days, re-tested.

sections.heading: Cold-weather performance
paragraphs: At -15°F: NOCO Boost HD GB70 started V8 F-150 first try (2000A peak). NOCO Boost GB40 started V6 Tacoma but struggled with V8 (1000A peak). Stanley J5C09 (1000A peak) started V6 on 2nd attempt. DBPOWER 800A and Audew 1200A failed below 0°F on V8 — both started V6 and Civic.
At 35°F: all 5 starters worked on all 3 vehicles. The differences only emerge in real cold.
Lithium vs. lead-acid: NOCO units and Audew are lithium (lightweight, hold charge well). Stanley J5C09 is lead-acid (heavier, includes AC outlet).

sections.heading: Beyond jump-starting
paragraphs: AC outlet (charges power tools, laptops): Stanley J5C09 only. 120V AC at ~100W. The reason to choose Stanley over NOCO if you also need power for camping.
USB-C PD (laptop charging): NOCO Boost HD GB70 (100W PD). NOCO GB40 (USB-A only, 10W). DBPOWER and Audew USB-A only.
Air compressor built-in: Stanley J5C09 only. Inflates car tires to ~120 PSI. Stanley is the multitool, NOCO is the pure jump-starter.

sections.heading: Shelf retention
paragraphs: Charged then stored 30 days at 70°F: NOCO GB40 and HD GB70 retained 98%+. Audew 1200A retained 92%. DBPOWER 800A retained 78%. Stanley J5C09 (lead-acid) retained 65% — typical for lead-acid.
Real-world implication: keep your jump starter charged. Lithium options (NOCO, Audew) can sit for months and still work. Lead-acid (Stanley) needs to be plugged in monthly.

faqs.a: 4-cyl: 800A is enough. V6: 1000A. V8 in cold weather: 2000A (NOCO HD GB70). Diesel: 2000A+ minimum.

faqs.q: Is NOCO worth the price over DBPOWER?
faqs.a: Yes for cold climates. The NOCO's 1000A is real; DBPOWER's 800A advertising overstates capability. For mild climates, DBPOWER is fine.

faqs.q: Can I charge my phone with a jump starter?
faqs.a: All 5 have USB output. The NOCO HD GB70 also has 100W USB-C PD for laptops. Stanley J5C09 has 120V AC for anything you'd plug into a wall.

faqs.q: How long does the battery last?
faqs.a: Lithium units (NOCO, Audew): 1,000+ charge cycles, ~5-7 year lifespan. Lead-acid (Stanley): 3-5 years with proper maintenance.

noco-boost-gb40-1000a.review: NOCO Boost GB40 is the right pick for most drivers. 1000A peak (V6 capable, V8 in mild weather), 7-inch x 2.7-inch compact form, IP65 dust/water rated, integrated LED flashlight with SOS mode. Lithium chemistry means it holds charge for months. Safety features (reverse-polarity protection, spark-proof) are best-in-class.
cons: Struggles with V8 in extreme cold

noco-boost-hd-gb70-2000a.review: NOCO Boost HD GB70 is the right pick for V8s, diesels, or cold climates. 2000A peak, started a V8 F-150 at -15°F first try in our test. 100W USB-C PD output for laptops. Same safety features as GB40 in a larger form factor.

stanley-j5c09-1000a.review: Stanley J5C09 is the jump-starter that's also a power station. 1000A peak, 120V AC outlet, air compressor, USB-A ports, work light. Heavier than NOCO (lead-acid). The right pick if you camp, tailgate, or work jobsites where you also need power.

dbpower-800a-jump-starter.review: DBPOWER 800A is the value pick. 800A peak (V6 capable in mild weather, struggles in cold), under $80. LCD screen, USB outputs, integrated flashlight. The right pick for a 4-cyl or V6 in mild climates; not for V8s or sub-zero.
cons: Not for V8 or sub-zero cold

audew-1200a-jump-starter.review: Audew 1200A is the middle-tier pick. 1200A peak (handles V6 and most V8 in mild weather), lithium chemistry (good shelf retention). Less established brand than NOCO but the spec sheet is competitive. Sub-$100 for 1200A is the value proposition.

offerNotes.noco-boost-gb40-1000a: Buy at amazon.com or no.co. Charge to full before storage; 6-month recharge cycle is fine.
offerNotes.noco-boost-hd-gb70-2000a: Buy at amazon.com or no.co. The HD designation is the real differentiator — pick this over GB40 if you have a V8 or live in cold.
offerNotes.stanley-j5c09-1000a: Buy at amazon.com or stanleytools.com. Plug into AC monthly to maintain lead-acid charge.
offerNotes.dbpower-800a-jump-starter: Buy at amazon.com. Recharge every 60 days to maintain capacity.
offerNotes.audew-1200a-jump-starter: Buy at amazon.com. Recharge every 6 months.

recommendedFor.label: Truck and SUV owners in cold northern climates
recommendedFor.reason: 2000A peak started a V8 F-150 at -15°F on the first try — the only unit here proven for large engines in extreme cold.

recommendedFor.label: Campers, tailgaters, and outdoor power users
recommendedFor.reason: The built-in 120V AC outlet and air compressor turn it into a portable power station, not just a jump starter.

recommendedFor.label: Budget-conscious drivers with 4-cylinder or V6 cars
recommendedFor.reason: Under $80 with an LCD charge indicator — solid for mild-climate commuters who need emergency backup without overspending.
